content:
When Apple finally responded to significantly higher costs for memory and other components, it pulled no punches. Some price increases exceeded 50%, while some memory and storage upgrades even doubled in price.

These higher prices are likely to persist for years, and may never come back down……

9to5Mac readers have long been skeptical about whether Apple will reduce prices once component supply constraints ease. More than two-thirds of readers said they expect these price hikes to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain pricing will not improve before 2028, and even when it does, the effect will be quite limited. The currently elevated pricing will persist for at least several years, and will most likely never return to previous levels — a conclusion that now seems obvious.

If this is indeed the case, how will you respond? Will you grit your teeth and continue buying Apple products at the same pace? Cut back on the number or frequency of Apple purchases? Or take other measures, such as buying a cheaper model, opting for a refurbished unit, or waiting for a price cut before making a move?

Feel free to take part in our poll, and share your thoughts in the comments section. The poll allows multiple selections, in case you plan to change your buying behaviour in more than one way.
